title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
This incident shows a deployed autonomous vehicle system operating outside the conditions it was designed for. Heavy traffic and road closures during Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco created extended periods of idling that drained batteries faster than the vehicles could be repositioned. The system had no mechanism to preemptively relocate vehicles away from high-congestion areas during predictable peak events, or to manage passengers stranded in vehicles with critically low battery levels.

The failure was not caught because Waymo did not model or test for the specific combination of extreme traffic volume, unplanned road closures, and thermal stress on batteries that occurred. Catching this would have required either simulation of major event scenarios before deploying in San Francisco, or operational protocols to remove vehicles from service hours before predicted gridlock. It also would have required protocols to address passengers in vehicles losing battery charge during an active ride.

It is not established whether the fire caused by a vehicle driving over fireworks reflects a separate design or operational gap, or was incidental to the main gridlock incident.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained in heavy traffic. Video evidence showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up after fireworks displays near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures. Waymo's roadside assistance team towed away the vehicles, and the company said it is evaluating ways to improve its resilience during heavy traffic events.

The gridlock also caused problems for passengers in active Waymo rides. One rider reported the vehicle continued driving during fireworks explosions on the street, while another passenger spent nearly two hours stuck in standstill traffic and witnessed people yelling at the driverless cars. Additionally, one Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries occurred. San Francisco's mayor and city officials acknowledged the traffic chaos and said they would discuss with public and private partners how to improve the situation for future events.
